question: According to ICD-11, a minimum symptom duration of one month is required to diagnose schizophrenia, whereas DSM-5 requires a minimum of six months.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. ICD-11 sets a one-month minimum duration; DSM-5 requires six months (including prodrome and residual phases). In India, the ICD-11 (formerly ICD-10) framework is the standard — a patient meeting one-month criteria would receive an ICD-11 schizophrenia diagnosis but might only meet DSM-5 criteria for schizophreniform disorder.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. ICD-11 requires core symptoms (e.g., first-rank or characteristic positive symptoms) for at least one month. DSM-5 sets a higher threshold — six months including prodromal and residual phases — making it more conservative. Remembering this difference matters when interpreting international literature and applying the correct diagnostic framework in India (ICD-11).
